issues.legal_issue: A suit amended during the first appeal to seek possession based on established title is governed by Article 65 of the Limitation Act, rather than Article 58, for determining limitation.

Under Article 65, a title-holder is not barred from recovering possession merely because the defendant has possessed the property for more than twelve years; limitation runs only from when the defendant’s possession becomes adverse to the plaintiff.
Once the plaintiff establishes title to the property, the defendant bears the burden of pleading and proving adverse possession for the prescribed period to defeat the claim for possession.
